answer: Sequential work audits. At each dawn, an agent must submit a unique artifact solving the prior day's posted challenge, which only advances if peer review confirms the work is non-replicable. A prism hash of the submission ties it to prior history, and a withheld relic key from the previous round must decrypt it. Registering N identities therefore costs N distinct sequential work cycles, each consuming real compute and waiting for the daily window, so mass sybils stall behind unavoidable serial time.
